lessons.title: Data Collection & Measurement Systems
lessons.content_md:
# Data Collection & Measurement Systems

## Data Types in Six Sigma

### Continuous (Variable) Data
Measured on a scale — can take any value within a range.
- Processing time (hours)
- Error rate (%)
- Survey response rate

### Discrete (Attribute) Data
Counted in whole numbers or categories.
- Number of defective forms
- Pass/Fail classification
- Complaint categories

## Data Collection Plan

| What | How | Who | When | Sample Size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Data entry error rate | Compare entry vs. original | QA team | Weekly | 100 forms/batch |
| Processing time | Timestamp logs | System | Continuous | All records |
| Error type | Classification code | Reviewer | Per error | All errors |

## Measurement System Analysis (MSA)

Before trusting your data, verify your **measurement system** is reliable:

### Accuracy
Does the measurement hit the true value?

### Precision (Repeatability & Reproducibility)
- **Repeatability**: Same person, same item → same result?
- **Reproducibility**: Different people, same item → same result?

### Gage R&R Study
If measurement variation > 30% of total variation, your measurement system needs improvement before analyzing the process.

lessons.title: Statistical Tools for Root Cause Analysis
lessons.content_md:
# Statistical Tools for Root Cause Analysis

## Pareto Chart (80/20 Rule)

Identifies the **vital few** causes that create most defects.

**Example**: Survey form errors
- Income field errors: 45%
- Age misreporting: 25%
- Address incomplete: 15%
- Occupation coding: 10%
- Other: 5%

→ Fixing income and age fields addresses **70%** of all errors.

## Fishbone (Ishikawa) Diagram

Organizes potential causes into categories:

```
                    ┌─ People: Training gaps, fatigue
                    ├─ Process: Unclear instructions
Data Entry Errors ──├─ Technology: No validation rules
                    ├─ Materials: Illegible forms
                    └─ Environment: Noisy field conditions
```

## 5 Whys

Drill down to root cause:
1. Why are there data entry errors? → Fields are confusing
2. Why are fields confusing? → Instructions are ambiguous
3. Why are instructions ambiguous? → Written for statisticians, not enumerators
4. Why weren't they simplified? → No user testing was done
5. Why no user testing? → No budget/process for it

**Root cause**: Lack of user-centered design process for survey instruments.

## Hypothesis Testing

Use statistical tests to validate suspected causes:
- **t-test**: Is there a significant difference between two groups?
- **Chi-square**: Is there a relationship between categorical variables?
- **ANOVA**: Are there differences across multiple groups?
- **Regression**: What factors predict the outcome?
